_note: Level 1 functional flow, generalized from the team's flood flow to all hazards. Function names keep the team's eight boxes. Latency allocations and derived L1 requirements are DRAFTS for the team to adjust; the team's own L1-L3 requirements take precedence.

hazards.name: Flooding
hazards.detect_example: River gauge reads water rising past its alert level

hazards.name: Fire
hazards.detect_example: Smoke sensor in the savanna belt trips; satellite hotspot from another system confirms

hazards.name: Illegal logging / deforestation
hazards.detect_example: Acoustic sensor hears a chainsaw; S-2 radar shows new canopy loss

hazards.name: Illegal mining / pollution
hazards.detect_example: Water-quality probe sees a turbidity spike below a mining zone

hazards.name: Wildlife and poaching
hazards.detect_example: Tagged elephant stops moving, or a gunshot is detected

hazards.name: Disease and community emergencies
hazards.detect_example: Ranger or health worker sends a priority report from a handheld

functions.name: DETECT
functions.description: A sensor, tag, ranger device or partner system detects an event that crosses a threshold and forms a short, time-stamped priority message.
functions.outputs: Priority message (<= a few hundred bytes)

functions.name: TRANSMIT to satellite
functions.description: The terminal sends the message to a satellite overhead, directly or through the nearest ranger-station tower when it sits under canopy.

functions.name: SEND to database
functions.description: The satellite downlinks to the nearest gateway; the regional database stores it, filters duplicates and forwards it to the Kinshasa hub, where it appears on the common operating picture (COP). Each node keeps a replica.

functions.name: PROCESS, evaluate threat
functions.description: Hub analysts and models fuse the event with other data (radar, weather, history) and decide whether it is a threat, where, and who is at risk.
functions.outputs: Threat assessment and recommended alert area

functions.name: AUTHORIZE
functions.description: The responsible national agency approves the alert and issues it as a CAP message. S-3 never decides; it only carries.
performed_by: National disaster or park agency (each of the 10 countries)

functions.name: RETRANSMIT to satellite
functions.description: The hub validates the CAP message, converts it to speech in the district's languages, sets the geo-target area and uplinks it to the broadcast satellite.

functions.name: SEND to outposts
functions.description: Community receivers and ranger-station loudspeakers inside the target area wake up and play the alert aloud; ranger terminals get the text.

functions.name: VERIFICATION
functions.description: Ranger stations confirm the alert was heard (receiver check-ins, patrols, the tower loudspeaker) and report ground truth; the acknowledgment returns over the satellite link and closes the loop to F4.

continuous_functions.name: Two-way responder communications
continuous_functions.description: Rangers and responders talk and text through the station, the satellite layer and commercial backhaul, without towers or the grid.

continuous_functions.name: Maintain the network
continuous_functions.description: Monitor terminal health and power (solar, hydro, hand crank), replace failed sensors and receivers, replenish satellites.

derived_L1_drafts.text: The system shall receive messages from terminals anywhere within the basin boundary, including terminals under 30-40 m canopy within relay range of a ranger station.
The space segment shall provide a satellite in simultaneous view of an open-sky terminal and a gateway within 18 min at the 95th percentile (threshold) and 2.5 min (objective).
The ground segment shall deliver a downlinked priority message to the hub COP within 10 min (threshold) and 2 min (objective) at >= 95% / >= 99% completeness.
Every database node shall hold a full replica and shall be able to run F3-F8 alone if the hub is unreachable.
The hub shall convert an authorized CAP alert into geo-targeted speech and put it on air within 4 min (threshold) and 1.25 min (objective).
The broadcast shall address areas of <= 50,000 km2 (threshold) / <= 2,500 km2 (objective) and carry French, Lingala, Kiswahili, Kikongo and Tshiluba.
Community receivers in the target area shall play the alert aloud within 6 min of broadcast (threshold), 1.75 min (objective), for >= 95% / >= 99% of receivers.
The community receiver shall cost <= $25, run from solar or hand crank, and receive with a fixed antenna needing no pointing.
Each ranger station shall return a delivery confirmation for its area within 6 h (threshold) and 15 min (objective).
The system shall support >= 500 simultaneous responder terminals at >= 4.8 kbps with all terrestrial networks down.
Ranger stations shall keep alerting and two-way service through 5 days without sun, using storage, micro-hydro where available, and hand crank.
No alert shall be broadcast without a valid CAP message signed by an authorized national agency.
